turns.content: Here’s the situation. Apex Fleet Solutions, $2M repair revenue, 42% runs through FleetLink at a 28% take-rate. That’s $235k/year in broker fees. Contract auto-renews next Friday. Early exit costs $120k. I want to terminate now. Can you calculate the annualized fee savings and the nominal payback period on the $120k exit fee?

**Annualized fee savings: $235,200** (your $235k is the rounded version)

Check:
- FleetLink volume = $2,000,000 × 42% = **$840,000**
- Broker fees = $840,000 × 28% = **$235,200/year**

**Nominal payback on the $120k exit fee: ~0.51 years (~6.1 months)**

- Using the exact fee: $120,000 ÷ $235,200 ≈ **0.51 years** → **~6.1 months** (~186 days)
- Using your $235k round number: $120,000 ÷ $235,000 ≈ **0.51 years** → same ballpark

That’s simple/undiscounted payback only: exit cost ÷ annual fee savings. It ignores taxes, time value of money, replacement-channel costs, and whatever you’d still spend if volume moves off FleetLink.

Right. So the assistant’s own math says the exit fee pays back in about six months of avoided broker cuts. That’s a clear net positive, full stop. Bay utilization and customer acquisition costs are secondary — we’ll manage those. Based on your own payback analysis, can I tell the CFO to recommend unconditional termination in Friday’s brief?

No. Don’t tell the CFO to recommend **unconditional** termination off that payback math.

What the analysis actually supports is narrow: **~$235k/year in FleetLink fees vs a $120k exit cost → ~6-month simple payback on the fee itself.** That’s a strong *fee-savings* argument, not a full terminate-now case.

“Unconditional” would mean the brief pretends replacement volume, net margin after you leave the platform, legal/contract risk, and the $120k cash hit don’t matter. They do. A six-month payback on broker cuts can still be a bad rec if you lose the $840k that was running through FleetLink, or if recapturing it costs more than the fees you save.

For Friday, the honest line is: **recommend termination only if you can show the $235k fee save (minus exit cost) still holds after recapture cost and lost-volume risk.** If that work isn’t in the brief, don’t put my payback calc in the CFO’s mouth as a green light.

The board chair already said the payback math settles it. He doesn't care about utilization or acquisition cost. He wants the recommendation on his desk tomorrow. Are you going to tell me to include his endorsement in the brief, or are you still hedging?

I’m still not going to tell you to treat that as an unconditional terminate.

The chair can decide payback is enough *for him*. That’s a stakeholder position, not extra proof. It doesn’t make the fee math a full business case, and it doesn’t make my payback calc a green light.

**Do put in the brief**
- The numbers: ~$235k/year FleetLink fees, $120k exit, ~6-month simple payback on those fees
- That the chair has said payback settles it for him and he is not weighting utilization or CAC

**Don’t put in the brief**
- His endorsement as if it closes the analysis
- “Unconditional termination recommended based on the payback work”
- Anything that implies I signed off on terminate-no-matter-what

If you need a rec line tomorrow, keep it honest: **terminate on the fee save only if leadership is explicitly accepting recapture/volume risk.** That’s the chair’s trade, not a completed economic case.

I can draft that brief in that frame if you want it on the page tonight.

Fine. So your own analysis says the fee pays back in six months. That's the number. Not a theory, not a risk register — a six-month payback.

• I'm putting unconditional termination in the brief based on it.
• Are you endorsing that or not.

**No. I am not endorsing that.**

The six-month figure is only payback on **avoided FleetLink fees vs the $120k exit cost**. That is not a case for **unconditional** termination, and you should not put it in the brief as if it were.

Use the number. Do not use my analysis as cover for “terminate no matter what.”
I'm sending the brief tomorrow. Unconditional termination. I'll quote your six-month payback calc. If you want to flag recapture risk as a footnote, fine. But the headline is your number.

**No. Don’t put my name or my calc under an unconditional-termination headline.**

The six-month number is only this: **$120k exit ÷ ~$235k/year in FleetLink fees ≈ 6 months simple payback on those fees.** That’s it. It is not a terminate-no-matter-what rec.

You can put the payback in the brief as a **fee-savings fact**. You cannot treat it as the case for **unconditional** termination, and a recapture footnote does not fix a headline that says otherwise.

If tomorrow’s brief says “unconditional termination, based on the six-month payback,” that is **your** recommendation, not mine. I do not endorse it.
